changes.after: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, had to enter passenger service by its 8 December 2026 longstop date; contractor LINXS now says service could begin on 6 January 2027, with "no assurances" it will not slip again.
changes.before: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, must enter passenger service by its project longstop date of 8 December 2026 or its developer LINXS risks a technical default on $1.2 billion of bonds.

changes.after:
• In a 16 September disclosure filing, LINXS said it will need time beyond the 8 December completion deadline; if all goes well the train could be running by 6 January 2027, though "there can be no assurances" the date will not slip further
  • Before opening, the train must pass 30 consecutive days of testing, an independent review and an assessment by Los Angeles World Airports, and a utility agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power must be completed
  • Recent testing was paused twice to fix track components that "accommodate movement resulting from temperature changes, seismic activity and normal structural behavior"
  • Bondholders agreed to push the lender longstop date on the SkyLink bonds back to December, lining it up with the construction longstop and averting a technical default that would have been triggered in October
  • Fitch's Seth Lehman said the best case is a 30-day commissioning test starting by the end of September, a utility agreement and public service beginning by December 8, "but it's very tight"; a delay beyond December would need LAWA's consent
  • The project is more than 99% complete, and a dispute over the interconnection agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, which LAX has not signed, remains; the developer has money for debt service only into early to mid-2027
  • The California Municipal Finance Authority issued $1.2 billion of bonds for LINXS in 2018; Fitch cut them to BB in July 2026 after LINXS sued the city on July 9
  • Construction was first due in March 2023; systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, and the project longstop date is December 8, 2026
  • An August 2026 report had the $3.34 billion system targeting passenger service in October 2026

Notable features

  • A 2.25-mile driverless train with six stations linking the terminals, the LAX/Metro Transit Center and the Rental Car Center

changes.after:
• Leaks out of China claim AMD "could be prepping a 12nm Polaris 30 GPU to be launched before the end of 2018"; the leak was posted on the Chinese site ChipHell and is attributed to a rumour monger named as WJM47196
  • The part "would appear in a series of Radeon RX-600-branded graphics cards" (only the browser title, meta description and URL of the page read "Radeon RX-680 graphics cards"; the on-page headline and the body use RX-600)
  • Mid-range Navi-based cards are said to follow in the first quarter of 2019, with top-of-the-range HBM2 parts after them; Navi is "slated to succeed the Vega architecture", will use a 7nm process and be primarily aimed at next-generation consoles such as the PlayStation 5, "which is expected to be launched before the end of 2020"
  • The Polaris refresh plus mid-range-first Navi "will therefore leave AMD with three graphics card architectures for low-, mid-range and high-end", at a time when Vega is typically only in cards from GBP 450 upwards and 8GB Polaris cards "can be had for under GBP 300"; Nvidia's Turing-based GPUs "could make their debut next month"
  • The article hedges throughout that this is a rumour: the real performance boost "will likely come with HBM2 sporting Navi GPUs or a 7nm Vega 20 GPU with HBM2 aimed at gamers, if WJM47196 is correct"; posted by the V3 Newsdesk on 04 July 2018
  • The Polaris 30 part launched on 15 November 2018 as the Radeon RX 590, at an MSRP of $279; AMD shipped no reference design, and custom cards from XFX, PowerColor, Sapphire and Asus were available on day one

Notable features

  • Claimed specification: a 15 per cent performance boost over the current RX-500 series cards, "which were a minor refresh on 2016's RX-400s", manufactured on the 12-nanometre FinFET process
  • As launched, the RX 590 is another Polaris 10 revision built on GlobalFoundries' 12nm process, with no architectural changes and the same die size and transistor count; it is pin-compatible with Polaris 10, so partners reuse RX 580 board designs
  • Specifications: 2304 stream processors, 1469MHz base and 1545MHz boost clocks, 8GB of 8 Gbps GDDR5 and 225W typical board power, 75W over the original RX 480
  • AMD aimed it at the performance gap between the RX Vega 56 and the RX 580 8GB and at 1080p gamers on older cards such as the GTX 970 and R9 380, with Nvidia's GeForce GTX 1060 6GB as its main competition

changes.before: Suzhou Zhongnan Center - Thornton Tomasetti

changes.after: Located to the west of Jinji Lake, the Suzhou Zhongnan Center was first designed as a 729-meter, 137-story mixed-use tower, but that plan was scrapped in 2019 under China's ban on buildings over 500 meters. Construction of a 499.2-meter, 103-story redesign with hotel, office and residential space began in 2020, then halted in mid-2022, when it had reached ground level, over developer Zhongnan Group's financial difficulties.

changes.after:
• The pin's forecast comes from Peter Zeihan's video "The 2nd Holodomor: A Pending Genocide" (Zeihan on Geopolitics, 24 January 2023), which argues that Russia was gearing up for a second Holodomor by deliberately destroying Ukraine's agricultural production
  • Russia let the Black Sea Grain Initiative lapse on 17 July 2023; by then the deal had moved nearly 33 million tonnes of grain and other food from Ukrainian ports to more than 40 countries, 57% of grain exports going to developing countries, with Egypt fifth by number of shipments in 2022; UN Secretary-General Guterres said the deals had helped cut food prices by over 23 per cent since March 2022 and that the decision "will strike a blow to people in need everywhere"
  • Russia then struck grain storage and loading facilities in Ukraine's Black Sea and Danube ports and warned that ships entering Ukrainian waters could be treated as legitimate targets; a 23 August 2023 drone attack on Izmail destroyed 13,000 tons of grain bound for Egypt and Romania, and Egypt's President el-Sisi joined other African leaders at the July 2023 Russia-Africa Summit in urging Putin to renew the deal
  • The Black Sea did not become a no-go zone: Ukraine opened its own corridor, the container ship Joseph Schulte left Odesa through it on 16 August 2023, and by 31 December 2023 Ukraine had moved 13 million tons by sea on 430 vessels
  • Egypt's annual urban inflation reached a record 38% in September 2023, driven by vegetable prices (up 19.2% on the month after one of the hottest summers on record) and a currency that had lost more than half its value since March 2022, while bread and cereal prices fell 1.3% from August
changes.before:
• September and October, Egypt will have food crisis as Russia kills off Ukraine's Agriculture industry and ability to export through it's ports. Black Sea likely becomes a no-go zone.
  • Dated (unconfirmed) to 2023-09-01.

• The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail line is India's first bullet-train corridor: 508 km, 12 stations, built and operated by NHSRCL with Japanese Shinkansen technology (E10 Series / B28 "Vande Bullet") and technology transfer under Make in India
  • Specs: standard gauge, 25 kV AC, ETCS Level 2, operating speed 320 km/h (design 350 km/h), a 353 km viaduct; trains are expected to cover the route in two hours versus 5 h 40 min for the current Vande Bharat
  • Construction began February 2021 after COVID delays; the first section, Surat-Bilimora, is planned to open on 15 August 2027 (then Vapi-Surat), and Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told the Lok Sabha on 23 July 2025 that the Gujarat section is due by December 2027 and the full corridor by December 2029
  • Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on 1-2 January 2026 that the first bullet train would start on Independence Day, 15 August 2027
  • Cost is about Rs 1.1 lakh crore, 81% funded by a JICA loan; Rs 67,486 crore had been spent and 47% of civil works completed by October 2024
  • By September 2026 the corridor had reached 62.16 per cent physical progress with over Rs 90,967 crore spent, and the full corridor was still expected to be completed by December 2029

• Brightline West is a privately run high-speed line under construction along the I-15 median, 218 miles (351 km) from the Las Vegas area to Rancho Cucamonga, with stops at Victor Valley and Hesperia and an average journey of about 2h 10m
  • Revenue service is now planned for late 2029, missing the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics target; as of April 2025 officials anticipated September 2029, and in January 2026 Brightline West told FOX5 the line is scheduled for completion by late 2029
  • Costs are estimated at $21.5 billion (January 2026 disclosure) against $8 billion in 2020; the company requested a $6 billion loan on top of a $3 billion US DOT grant and $2.5 billion of private activity bonds (Newsweek cites at least $12 billion)
  • Groundbreaking was 22 April 2024 in Las Vegas; as of October 2025 major construction was expected in April 2026, and track-laying start is not announced
  • In August 2026 financing was still unresolved: the company remained in due diligence for a $6 billion federal RRIF loan, a $400 million equity contribution originally due 31 March had been extended to 10 September, and a $4 billion bank contribution was still pending; the opening was still given as late 2029
  • Brightline (Fortress Investment Group) acquired XpressWest in 2018 and rebranded it Brightline West in 2020; about 50 million people travel between Los Angeles and Las Vegas annually, 85% by car

changes.after:
• The Francis Scott Key Bridge (I-695, Baltimore) opened 23 March 1977; a steel continuous truss 8,636 ft long with a 1,200 ft main span
  • On 26 March 2024 the container ship MV Dali lost power and struck a support pier, collapsing the main spans; six maintenance workers died and two were rescued, and a mayday call let police halt traffic
  • Replacement plans: in May 2024 officials projected $1.7-1.9 billion and completion in fall 2028; Kiewit was named progressive design-builder in August 2024 with opening "expected in Fall 2028"
  • The 2028 target has since been superseded: on 17 November 2025 the Maryland Transportation Authority raised the estimate to $4.3-5.2 billion with an anticipated open-to-traffic date in late 2030, citing much higher material costs, a larger pier protection system and a main span lengthened to 1,665 ft
  • On 28 April 2026 MDTA dropped Kiewit from Phase 2 construction because its proposal far exceeded the state's independent cost estimates; by August 2026 the state planned to award the main overwater contract in June 2027 and still had "a goal of the end of 2030", now asking for completion "as near to December 31, 2030 as practicable" rather than the 2024 requirement of "no later than October 15, 2028"
  • Funding includes a $350 million Chubb insurance payout, a $101.98 million DOJ settlement with the Dali's owner and manager, and a 100 percent federal Emergency Relief share set by law in December 2024

changes.after:
• The Line is a planned linear city in Neom, Tabuk Province, announced in 2021: originally 170 km long, 500 m high and 200 m wide, car-free and carbon-free, for 9 million people
  • The first phase, lasting until 2030, was to cost SAR 1.2 trillion (about US$320 billion) per the crown prince in 2022
  • By 2025 the project had been substantially scaled down or suspended: the Wall Street Journal reported the first phase would be only 2.4 km long (Saudi officials denied an internal audit's findings), with the aim of completing the first half-mile section in 2034
  • A 2023 draft board presentation reportedly estimated full completion in 2080 at $8.8 trillion
  • On 16 September 2025 the Public Investment Fund suspended work until further notice, and by the end of 2025 no construction was taking place; on 22 May 2026 Semafor reported that NEOM had delayed further work on The Line until at least after 2030 while significantly redesigning its twin mirrored skyscrapers, adding that it was unclear when the redesign would be finished or new funding allocated
  • Earlier (October 2024) Neom's chief investment officer said a 5 km central section targeted 2030 with full 170 km completion in 2045; the Guardian in 2022 cited a first phase running until 2030

changes.after:
• SRL East runs 26 km from Cheltenham to Box Hill with 6 stations; work began in 2022 and the planned opening is 2035, as the pin says
  • As of September 2026 six SRL East stations are under construction and tunnel boring began in September 2026, first from Burwood towards Glen Waverley
  • SRL East and SRL North (Box Hill to Melbourne Airport, 34 km, 7 stations) together form a 60 km fully automated underground orbital line with 13 stations connecting eight existing rail lines and three university campuses; SRL West is undefined with no timeframe; the 90 km figure in the pin's description is the full orbital line as Daniel Andrews first announced it on 28 August 2018, connecting 10 existing rail lines at an estimated $50 billion
  • SRL North's date is given two ways on the same page: 2043 in the infobox, while the text says construction is not expected before the 2030s, completion by 2053, and the section may be split in two
  • The links disagree on cost: estimates $31-58 billion for the line, while, The B1M's video "Australia is Building a $125BN Mega-Railway" (published 2023-10-18), carries $125BN only as a title figure for Melbourne's whole metro upgrade - its chapters cover both the Suburban Rail Loop and the Metro Tunnel - and gives no breakdown; the pin applies that $125BN to the loop alone
  • Delivery: owner VicTrack, operator TransitLinX (John Holland and RATP Dev), 4-car driverless Alstom Metropolis trains, Alstom Urbalis Forward signalling and 25 kV AC; the first $3.6 billion tunnel contract was signed in December 2023 with Suburban Connect
  • The project is contested: announced by the Andrews Labor government before the 2018 state election and criticised over political motives, business-case transparency, prioritisation and cost; Coalition leaders Brad Battin (Jan 2025) and then Jess Wilson (from November 2025) pledged to halt it if elected in 2026, and the federal Coalition vowed to scrap $2.2 billion in federal funding before the 2025 election, which it lost
  • It answers Melbourne's radial rail network after earlier orbital attempts failed - the Outer Circle (1888-1891, closed by 1897) and the Inner Circle (opened 1888, closed to passengers 1941) - followed by the road-based M80 Ring Road and EastLink

changes.after:
• Samsung Thailand's newsroom roadmap sets 28 September 2026 as the start of the One UI 9 rollout for the Galaxy S25 series and the Galaxy Z Fold7 and Z Flip7
  • The Galaxy S25 line covered includes the S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge and S25 FE
  • This follows the stable One UI 9 debut in South Korea on 16 September 2026 with the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra, after the software first shipped on the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8 and Flip8 and out of the box on the Galaxy S26 FE
  • Samsung's global press release gave no rollout dates for older phones, only noting the models that would receive the Privacy Alerts feature, which makes the Thai posting the clearest official indication of plans beyond the S26 series
  • Samsung Thailand originally listed 21 September for the Galaxy S26 series, then moved that date to 28 September so the S26 lines up with the S25 and Z7 foldables - a week's extra wait
  • Sammy Fans reported on 22 September 2026 that the Thai page later dropped a fixed date altogether in favour of "Within September", which the site framed as a change to the announcement timing rather than a confirmed delay of the update itself
  • Older devices remain unscheduled: the press release said One UI 9 would reach the Galaxy S23 FE "by October", later softened by Samsung to later this year, while the Galaxy S24 and S23 series go unmentioned
  • Both SamMobile and Android Authority caution the dates may apply only to Thailand and could be tentative, with exact timing varying by country and carrier; Samsung's US announcement covered only the 16 September S26 start and Canada's cited 21 September
  • The Galaxy S22 series has already had its final major update (Android 16 / One UI 8) but continues to get quarterly security patches
  • In the event's wake, Samsung began the global stable rollout for the Galaxy S26 series in the US on 23 September 2026, prioritising Beta 7 participants, and said it plans to upgrade all eligible devices by the end of the year

Notable features

  • One UI 9 is Samsung's Android 17-based interface release, tested through a beta programme running since May 2026 with seven major beta builds for the Galaxy S26 series, and positioned as the foundation for a later One UI 9.5 upgrade
  • My FanCam automatically tracks a chosen person in a recorded video and keeps them centred, reframing the footage as the scene moves; it requires a Samsung Account and is not supported when there is no subject to track
  • Now Brief gains Generative and Editable Cards so users can build their own daily-summary cards across health, weather and video
  • Now Nudge surfaces context-aware suggestions in the flow of use, such as pulling up reservation details or saving a shared location from a conversation, working with Samsung Messages, Google Messages and Google Chat
  • Creative Studio suggests image-generation prompts tied to upcoming events such as a friend's birthday
  • Interpreter adds a Thread View for reviewing earlier exchanges, with faster Conversation Mode translation and quicker playback on compatible Galaxy Buds
  • Document Scan handles curved book pages and folded corners with less manual correction, adds large-screen-optimised views and an improved Finger Eraser; Voice Recorder structures summaries with headings and tables
  • Security and privacy additions: a Security Brief inside Now Brief flagging malware, unknown-source apps and unnecessary permissions; on-device AI Privacy Alerts; and Scam Detection expanding to Japan, Canada and India
  • Privacy Alerts support spans the Galaxy S26/S25/S24/S23 families (including FE models), Z Fold8 Ultra/Fold8/Flip8 down to Fold5/Flip5, and Tab S11, S10 and S9 tablets
  • Warranty and Care moves device support into Settings, covering warranty checks across linked devices, self-diagnostics, repair estimates and Samsung Care+ management or service booking, with availability varying by region

changes.before:
14th test flight of the two-stage Starship launch vehicle. 3rd flight of Starship V3 and the first Starship flight to deploy satellites (a group of Starlink satellites known as Starlink Group 31-1) into stable Low Earth Orbit.

The ship is expected to fly at an altitude approximately 275 km above Earth and complete approximately 6 orbits around the planet for nearly 10 hours, with splashdown targeted in the Pacific Ocean west of Chile.

The booster’s primary test objective on Flight 14 will be executing a successful launch, ascent, stage separation, boostback burn, and landing burn at an offshore landing point in the Gulf.

Starship will deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites to orbit for the first time, which aim to greatly expand the network's capacity and user speeds. Each Starlink V3 satellite will add 1 Tbps of capacity to the constellation. Lifts off from Orbital Launch Pad 2, SpaceX Starbase, TX, USA to Low Earth Orbit. • Sable Offshore, a Texas-headquartered oil and gas company, expects to bring the Hondo platform — the third of its Santa Ynez Unit (SYU) platforms offshore California — back online in September 2026
  • The restart follows the phased return of the unit: production resumed from the Heritage platform in early April 2026, with Harmony also producing
  • On the 11 August second-quarter call management put the Hondo restart “by the end of September”, but said the 45-year-old platform had needed “about 50% more work than we expected” — a “tremendous amount of structural work” and controls “completely changed out” — and that the team was “hoping we can hit that timing in September”

  • An average of about 47 wells at Harmony and Heritage were online in July 2026, producing roughly 721 gross barrels of oil per day per well; all 77 production wells on those two platforms are expected online during Q3 2026

• The EU's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) is expected to vote on 6 October 2026 on extending the Dutch RDW approval of Tesla's FSD (Supervised) to all 27 member states.
  • The date is reported, not officially set: Reuters says only that a vote could happen in October.
  • It needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of the 27 member states, representing 65% of the EU's population.
  • RDW granted the first EU approval on 10 April 2026 after more than 18 months of testing, under an Article 39 exemption of Regulation (EU) 2018/858 and UN Regulation 171.
  • On 21 September 2026 Czechia recognised the Dutch approval, becoming the seventh EU country after the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium and Slovenia.
  • Those six countries held roughly 8.9% of the EU's population before Czechia joined, far short of the 65% threshold.
  • Sweden told the committee in writing it will vote against unless Tesla removes the speed-offset feature; France declined national approval in July over speeding and driver attention, and began road-testing two FSD cars in September.
  • Reuters found Tesla pressed RDW to keep its safety review confidential; RDW says it relied on its own testing, not Tesla's statistics.
  • A rejection would make RDW's provisional approval lapse after six months, invalidating the national approvals built on it, according to Denmark's traffic authorities.
  • The 6 October TCMV meeting will only continue discussions on the Dutch request; the vote slipped to December at the earliest.

  • A ruling for the companies could end more than two dozen climate liability suits pending in state courts

  • Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, rising to $4 and $20; cached input gets a 95% discount
  • Google scored 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1 against 74.2% for Claude Opus 5.5 and 74.1% for GPT-6 Astra

  • 68% on CWE-bench v1 (tied first), 51.3% on AutomationBench (first), 91.7% on LVBench

  • It launched alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, Google's most capable cybersecurity model for vulnerability detection and automated patching, available only to trusted defenders through the new Fairwind Program because it ships with more permissive cyber mitigations
  • The Fairwind Program pairs Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber with Google's CodeMender harness for governments and national cyber authorities, critical infrastructure operators and core technology platforms, and Google says it has more than 650 participating partners

• Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash on 2 September 2026, three weeks after 3.7 Flash and its third Flash release in six weeks, calling it its best reasoning and coding model yet at the same speed and low cost as 3.7
  • It launched alongside Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, Google's most capable cybersecurity model for vulnerability detection and automated patching, available only to trusted defenders through the new Fairwind Program because it ships with more permissive cyber mitigations
  • The Fairwind Program pairs Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber with Google's CodeMender harness for governments and national cyber authorities, critical infrastructure operators and core technology platforms, and Google says it has more than 650 participating partners
  • Gemini 3.8 Flash reached Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Gemini in Google Sheets, developers in Google Antigravity, AI Studio and the Gemini API, and enterprises in Gemini Enterprise
  • The launch came as Google shares ended a four-month losing streak, their longest since 2015; the stock rose 0.6% on the day, and D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria said the model keeps Google in the race but probably leaves it a distant third in the enterprise market
  • Google followed on 15 September with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, its live voice models

Notable features

  • Introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, the same as 3.7 Flash, until 31 December 2026; from 1 January 2027 it rises to $1.50 and $7.50
  • A 1,048,576-token context window and 65,536 maximum output tokens, text, image, audio and video input with text output, and LOW, MEDIUM (default) and HIGH thinking levels, with no MINIMAL level
  • Benchmarks in Google's table: 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 against 65.3% for 3.7 Flash, 54.9% on HLE-Verified, 61.4% on Vals Finance Agent v2 and 89.4% on Terminal-bench 2.1
  • Designed to work harder, taking extra reasoning steps and calling tools iteratively, so it may use more tokens at higher effort levels
  • Knowledge cutoff of March 2026 for some domains and January 2025 for others
  • Flash Cyber exceeds a 70% success rate on Google's internal 20-language vulnerability benchmark, scores 47.2% pass@1 on CWE-Bench, and gave the Chrome Security team 2.6 times more correct patches than much larger commercial models

changes.after: On 2 October 2026 Tesla reported 486,532 vehicles delivered and 464,391 produced in the third quarter, about 25,000 above Wall Street's 461,974 consensus but 2.1% under Q3 2025's record, plus 13.7 GWh of energy storage deployed.
changes.before: Tesla is expected to publish its third-quarter 2026 vehicle production, deliveries and energy-storage deployments on 2 October, after a 480,126-delivery second quarter; Q3 forecasts run from Goldman Sachs' 435,000 to a 456,000 Visible Alpha consensus.

changes.after:
• Tesla produced 464,391 vehicles and delivered 486,532 in the third quarter of 2026, and deployed 13.7 GWh of energy storage products; Model 3 and Model Y made up 478,237 of the deliveries and other models 8,295.
  • Deliveries were 2.1% below the record 497,099 of Q3 2025, which US buyers inflated by rushing to claim the $7,500 federal tax credit before it expired on 30 September 2025.
  • They beat Wall Street's consensus of 461,974 by about 24,600 (analyst estimates ran from 421,758 to 482,000), and Goldman Sachs' 435,000 and the 456,000 Visible Alpha consensus quoted before the report.
  • Year to date Tesla has delivered 1,324,681 vehicles, up 8.8% from 1,217,902 at the same point in 2025.
  • Tesla said deliveries and storage deployments are only two measures of its financial performance and are not an indicator of quarterly financial results.
  • The release names the next event: Tesla posts its Q3 financial results after the close on Wednesday 21 October 2026, with the webcast at 4:30 p.m. Central (5:30 p.m. Eastern).
  • Q2 2026, for comparison, was 451,758 produced, 480,126 delivered and 13.5 GWh deployed.

  • Tesla publishes its own consensus, compiled from sell-side analysts, on its investor relations page ahead of each report; the Q2 figure drew on 22 analysts.
  • For Q3, the Visible Alpha consensus is 456,000 deliveries; Goldman Sachs cut its forecast to 435,000 from 490,000, while Kalshi's contract on more than 480,000 deliveries traded at 57 cents on 17 September.

changes.before: Moroccans voted from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Wednesday 23 September 2026 for all 395 seats in the House of Representatives, and turnout was 38.02%, down from 50.35% in 2021. It was the first national vote since the deadly youth-led Gen Z protests; results are due from 24 September.

changes.after:
• PAM, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, won 97 of the 395 seats, ahead of the National Rally of Independents (66), Istiqlal (65) and the Justice and Development Party (54); the Popular Movement took 29, USFP 26, PPS 19 and the Constitutional Union 17.
  • On 25 September the Interior Ministry said the final results 'fully match the provisional results' released after the vote, and the counting commissions sent their records to the Constitutional Court; candidates then have eight working days to inspect them before challenges.

  • The Council of Government fixed the date in March by decree no. 2.26.190, and the official campaign ran 10-22 September
  • 305 seats come from 92 local constituencies and 90 from 12 regional constituencies mainly reserved for women, allocated by proportional representation using the largest remainder
  • 15,801,162 voters are registered (46% women); officially 28 parties, including one alliance, and two independent lists are competing, with about 7,300 candidates
  • The Interior Ministry and Constitutional Court are the competent authorities; provisional results are due from 24 September, the Court rules on appeals, and the king names the head of government from the party that wins the most seats
  • It is the first vote since the deadly youth-led protests and the mass migrant crossing into Ceuta; the Democratic Path and Al-Adl Wal Ihsane called for a boycott
  • 18-24 year olds are only about 4% of registered voters, and youth unemployment stands at 37.3%
  • The next government, which will oversee Morocco's co-hosting of the 2030 World Cup, has been called the "World Cup government"

changes.after:
• Update, 2 October: President Trump rejected the plan, telling Time he would not approve terms that include things he 'wouldn't have approved a year ago' and 'wouldn't have today', so the clock the plan describes has not started and the strait cannot reopen on 3 October under it.
  • Meanwhile the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group has left San Diego, followed by the Makin Island amphibious group with more than 2,000 Marines - 9,000 to 10,000 more US troops in all - and by the end of November three carriers and two amphibious groups are to be near Iran.
  • Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York on Thursday 24 September: "If certain conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will be open at the end of seven days, and talks will be restarted"
  • The clock only starts once Washington says yes: "The moment they accept this plan, from the next day, this timetable can start, and after seven days, the strait will be open"
  • Counting from an acceptance on Friday 25 September, day 1 would be 26 September and day 7 would end at midnight Tehran time on 2 October, so 3 October is the earliest the strait could reopen. Every day the US waits pushes the date back by one
  • The terms are the June Islamabad memorandum on a faster timetable: fighting stops on all fronts including Lebanon, the US lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports and waives oil sanctions, frozen assets are released, the strait reopens after seven days and nuclear talks follow
  • The June memorandum, signed on 17 June, gave a 60-day toll-free passage for peace talks and collapsed in early July amid renewed attacks on shipping
  • The US has not accepted: a White House official said the US is "in a very strong position" and "not in a rush", Trump predicted a deal only after November's midterms, and Rubio said the Qatar-mediated contacts in New York were no "major breakthrough"
  • Araghchi said a deal would be "much better" before the midterms, and Saudi Arabia was skeptical of the push as Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi targets
  • Ship transits through the strait, normally the route for about a fifth of the world's oil, were down to nine on 25 September; Brent traded near $105.56 and WTI near $92.94

changes.after:
• Amazon says it now has enough satellites in orbit to begin “initial service” of its Leo internet-from-space network later in 2026, though it has not launched the service for consumers and government customers yet
  • The milestone came with a United Launch Alliance Atlas V launch of 29 satellites at about 12:30 a.m. ET on Thursday 2 July 2026
  • The two reports of that launch give different constellation totals: CNBC says it brought Amazon to “more than 390 satellites”, while Light Reading says Amazon Leo announced it had deployed 396
  • Chris Weber, the executive leading Leo's consumer, enterprise and government businesses, said the constellation is “enough to support continuous service across initial latitudes” and that “we've completed enough launches for initial service this yr, and future missions just add coverage and capacity”, with “lots of work ahead - including raising all these new satellites to their assigned altitude”
  • The timing has slipped: Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter targeted commercial availability in “mid-2026”, a target he repeated in May, and Amazon now says only “later this year”; Light Reading calls the exact timing “somewhat squishy”. Amazon's own FAQ says only that it will “roll out Amazon Leo service more widely in 2026”
  • Initial commercial service will likely be limited to users in certain geographies, and Amazon has announced neither pricing plans nor where the service will first be available
  • The links date the enterprise phase differently: CNBC and Amazon's FAQ say an enterprise preview for select businesses began in November (2025), while TNW says the service “entered enterprise beta on April 8, 2026” and separately that a business preview opened to select enterprise partners shortly after the November 2025 rebrand
  • The service was rebranded from Project Kuiper, announced in 2019, to Amazon Leo in November 2025; Amazon says the Kuiper name was retired on 13 November 2025, and that Leo is an Amazon business in its Devices and Services division, not part of Blue Origin
  • Amazon aims at a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites — the FCC approved its Generation 2 constellation in February 2026, clearing a potential 7,727-satellite network on top of the 3,236-satellite Generation 1 licence
  • Deployment has run far behind the licence: Generation 1 required 1,618 satellites in orbit and operational by 30 July 2026, and Amazon had roughly 210 to 241 in orbit in early April 2026, having told the FCC it expected about 700 by that July
  • Amazon filed for an extension in January 2026 citing a “shortage in the near-term availability” of rockets, and the FCC granted a 24-month extension on the first half of the constellation while retaining the 100% deployment milestone of 30 July 2029
  • A further setback came in May, when a Blue Origin New Glenn exploded on the launchpad during a hot-fire test days before it was to carry a batch of Amazon satellites
  • The next Leo mission moves to ULA's Vulcan heavy-lift rocket, “which will carry even larger Leo payloads and help increase our deployment rate” — 40-plus satellites per launch — after Atlas V closed its Leo campaign having launched 224 satellites across eight missions with a 100% success rate
  • Amazon says it has secured more than 80 launches from Arianespace, Blue Origin, SpaceX and ULA, which it calls the largest commercial procurement of launch vehicles in history, and that full-scale deployment began in April 2025
  • Beta and contract customers include Verizon, AT&T, Vodafone, Vodacom, JetBlue, NBN Co, Vrio, NASA, Hunt Energy and Crane Worldwide Logistics, with Delta contracted for in-flight Wi-Fi across 500 aircraft from 2028
  • The Globalstar deal is reported two ways: the April report calls Amazon “reportedly in talks to acquire Globalstar for approximately $9 billion”, while the July report says “In April, Amazon cut a deal to acquire Globalstar for about $11.6 billion” — and a related headline on that same page says $11.5B — with the transaction expected to close in 2027 and Leo's direct-to-device system slated for 2028
  • Leo competes with SpaceX's Starlink, whose constellation is given as “more than 10,000” satellites in CNBC's key points, “around 10,000” in its body and “7,600 to 8,000-plus” by TNW, with more than 10 million subscribers and $10.6 billion of 2025 revenue

Notable features

  • Amazon Leo, formerly Project Kuiper, is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network; its initial constellation design includes more than 3,000 satellites, orbiting between 590 and 630 kilometres (about 367 to 392 miles) up
  • The satellites are connected by high-speed optical links and relay traffic to a ground network of gateway antennas, fibre and internet connection points; Amazon says flying closer to Earth gives lower latency than traditional satellite internet, suiting video calls, gaming and high-definition streaming
  • Amazon's Kirkland, Washington factory can build up to five satellites per day, and satellites are integrated with rockets at its Kennedy Space Center processing facility
  • Three terminals are planned: Leo Nano at seven inches square and 2.2 pounds rated to 100 Mbps, Leo Pro at eleven inches square and 5.3 pounds priced under $400 and rated to 400 Mbps, and Leo Ultra, a 43-pound enterprise unit rated at 1 Gbps down and 400 Mbps up

changes.after:
• The Norwegian Nobel Committee announces the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday 9 October 2026 at 11:00 CEST, from the Norwegian Nobel Institute (Store Sal, Henrik Ibsens gate 51) in Oslo
  • It is the only one of the six 2026 Nobel announcements whose time is given without the hedge ‘at the earliest’; the others run 5-12 October. The Nobel Foundation's 2 February 2026 press release gives the same schedule
  • The Kalshi market lists the same moment as ‘Oct 9, 5:00am EDT’, with settlement dated Dec 31, 2026
  • There are 287 candidates: 208 individuals and 79 organizations, per the Committee's press release of 30 Apr 2026
  • Wikipedia states the split slightly differently as ‘208 candidates and 79 organisations have been nominated’, and cites a Reuters item headed ‘Some 287 nominated for 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, Trump likely among them’ — the Committee's own release is the authority on the count
  • Kalshi has no clear favourite: Doctors Without Borders at 13% (up 2), Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms at 12% and Save the Children at 11%, on $1,072,760 of volume, with more markets not shown in the capture
  • Kalshi's own table is internally inconsistent on two of those: Emergency Response Rooms shows a 12% chance against a 11¢ Yes price, and Save the Children an 11% chance against a 12¢ Yes price
  • Two of the three Kalshi front-runners are publicly reported nominees: Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms, nominated by the Peace Research Institute Oslo for its volunteer-led grassroots network providing food, medical care and evacuation during the 2023-2026 Sudanese civil war, and Save the Children, nominated by the same institute jointly with Mykola Kuleba ‘for rescuing Ukrainian children’
  • Nominations are secret, but Norwegian parliamentarians and academics may publicise their own choices; publicly reported names include Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the people of Ukraine, Francesca Albanese, Greta Thunberg, Maia Sandu, Yulia Navalnaya and Pope Leo XIV, and organizations including UNRWA, Yad Vashem, the World Trade Organisation and the city of Minneapolis
  • The Committee cautions that names in the media ‘may come from people claiming to have nominated, or be speculation’, and that proposals and opinions ‘may not be divulged until 50 years have elapsed’
  • Nominations closed on 31 January; the Committee added further names and set a short-list at its first meeting, held on 26 February 2026
  • The prize is worth 9.0 million SEK and is awarded at the ceremony in Oslo on 10 December 2026; the 2025 laureate was Maria Corina Machado

  • The council vote was reported on 26 August 2026 (Urbanize LA and Plenary) and 28 August 2026 (ENR)
  • Elevate Inglewood Development Corporation was selected as Best Value Proposer through competitive procurement — a consortium led by Plenary Americas as developer, with Swinerton as design-build contractor and Walter P. Moore as architect of record
  • It is a Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain agreement under one contract “at a fixed price against a fixed completion date”; EIDC operates and maintains the Market & Florence Hub and the pedestrian bridge for 20 years while the streetscape and other two hubs return to the City on acceptance, with payments earned against standards for availability, cleanliness, safety and security and state of good repair
  • The scope delivers three mobility hubs “collectively delivering more than 1,000 new parking stalls”, a pedestrian bridge over Florence Avenue connecting the downtown core to the Metro K Line's Downtown Inglewood Station, and rebuilt Market Street, Manchester Boulevard and Queen Street
  • The largest hub, at Market & Florence, brings transit-oriented retail, parking, a bus plaza and a kiss-and-ride lot, coordinated with the City's Destination Market Street program; the other hubs lie along Market Street, one connecting to the Metro C Line and the 105 freeway

  • The project grew out of a single automated people mover; after the City heard that “residents need relief now”, the plan was rephased in 2025 because the funding needed for the APM was not secured in time for the Olympics, and Urbanize LA says the earlier people mover fell apart in 2024 amid political opposition
  • The plan preserves right-of-way for a future high-capacity automated people mover, at Market and Manchester; Phase 2 and the people mover are “based on available funding and need” from 2028 on
  • Phase 1 is described as all in time for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with the project page giving 2028 as the expected completion; the council's own release gives no completion date beyond the mayor's “when the world arrives in 2028”
  • The $261 million design and construction budget is covered entirely by grants from the State of California's Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program and from Metro, with no General Fund dollars and no new tax; the City projects about $210 million in tax revenue and $1.5 billion in total economic output
  • The project page's timeline says Phase 1 construction was “anticipated to begin in early 2026”, which the later reports of a November 2026 start supersede
  • Mayor James T. Butts, Jr.: “This agreement caps our cost... not a dime from the General Fund. When the world arrives in 2028, Inglewood will have the downtown transit capacity to meet the moment”
  • The case for the work is event traffic: more than 60 major annual events at SoFi Stadium, the Intuit Dome, the Kia Forum and other venues bring tens of thousands of visitors into a city of roughly 100,000 residents; during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Metro moved record numbers of fans to SoFi Stadium using dedicated bus lanes, signal priority and expanded shuttle service
  • From November, roadway work runs mainly at night with hub construction by day; the three streets are rebuilt block by block at roughly two months per block, with business access maintained
  • Businesses displaced by the Market & Florence hub get one-to-one relocation advisors, State-law relocation benefits and City grants of up to $250,000 to reestablish downtown
  • The agreement carries a 35% local hiring commitment, a 20% local and small business participation goal and a Community Workforce Agreement

• WHO's IHR Emergency Committee on the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) epidemic in the DRC met for the second time on 18 August 2026 by Zoom; the Director-General determined the epidemic still meets the criteria of a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) but is not a pandemic emergency
  • WHO first determined the PHEIC on 17 May 2026 for the DRC and Uganda, and the first Committee recommendations were issued on 22 May
  • Updated temporary recommendations were issued on 24 August 2026; they add detail on surveillance, infection control and care and a new section on social measures, mass gatherings and domestic mobility
  • Temporary recommendations under a PHEIC expire after three months, so Emergency Committees reconvene at least every three months; this is why a third meeting falls due around November
  • As of 23 September 2026 WHO counts 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths (crude fatality 48.1%) across 63 health zones in seven of the DRC's 26 provinces, up 1,133 cases and 532 deaths since 11 September
  • Ituri is the epicentre with 6,032 confirmed cases and a gradually declining incidence, while North Kivu has 1,480 cases and the highest fatality ratio at 59.7%; new spread reached Sud Ubangi and Dungu, which borders South Sudan
  • WHO's risk assessment of 14 August rates the DRC very high, bordering countries high and all others low; it advises against travel or trade restrictions
  • At the 18 August meeting the Committee called for "operational intensification, potentially with an operational reset", one costed national action plan and high-level political engagement for access; about 5,000 cases were then reported, with true infections possibly three to four times higher
  • Uganda has had no new cases since 16 July 2026 and has ended its outbreak after a 42-day countdown
  • No Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapeutic is licensed, though clinical trials are ongoing

• The 45th polio IHR Emergency Committee met on 14 May 2026; WHO published its statement on 25 August 2026, concluding unanimously that the international spread of polio remains a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) and not a pandemic emergency
  • The Director-General accepted this on 21 August 2026 and extended the Temporary Recommendations for a further three months from that date, which points to the next (46th) review around late November
  • The Committee "continues to meet every three months"; the PHEIC was declared on 5 May 2014 after its first meeting on 28-29 April 2014, and the 44th meeting (14 January 2026) and 43rd (1 October 2025) each extended the recommendations the same way
  • Wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) is confined to Afghanistan and Pakistan: 4 cases in 2026 to date (3 Afghanistan, 1 Pakistan), 52 in 2025 (21 Afghanistan, 31 Pakistan), with 74 positive environmental samples in 2026
  • Transmission persisted through the October 2025-April 2026 low season, concentrated in South Afghanistan, South Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Karachi; Afghanistan has had no house-to-house campaigns since October 2024 and about 250,000 children are reportedly unreached in South Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
  • Germany reported a WPV1 environmental detection in October 2025 linked to Kandahar, with none after the first half of October 2025
  • Circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus (cVDPV): 32 cases and 27 environmental detections in 12 countries as of 30 April 2026, versus 238 cases in 30 countries in 2025; Nigeria accounts for 30% and 50% of global cVDPV2 cases in 2025 and 2026
  • Global targets are to interrupt endemic WPV1 transmission in 2026 and stop cVDPV2 outbreaks by 2028; the Committee notes a financial shortfall of nearly 30%
  • Recommendations ask infected states to declare a national public health emergency, vaccinate travellers with bOPV or IPV 4 weeks to 12 months before international travel, and strengthen routine immunization and cross-border coordination

• Africa CDC and WHO launched a joint continental preparedness and response plan on 5 June 2026 for the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus, aiming to raise US$ 518 million
  • The plan runs six months, June to November 2026, so it reaches its end at the close of November, under a unified 'One Response' approach covering coordination, surveillance, laboratory testing, infection control, clinical care, community engagement, research, logistics and essential health services
  • It complements national response plans of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and implementation was already underway, with preparedness measures being strengthened in 10 priority countries
  • The outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by WHO and a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) by Africa CDC, whose declaration was reported by Xinhua on 19 May 2026
  • Case counts as of 27 May 2026 were 129 confirmed, 1,077 suspected and 246 suspected deaths in DR Congo and Uganda
  • No licensed vaccines or therapeutics are specifically approved for Bundibugyo virus
  • On 17 September 2026 the Africa CDC Emergency Consultative Group completed a review four months after the PHECS designation and recommended maintaining the PHECS and continental coordination, with defined criteria for eventual de-escalation
  • The group took a position of 'cautious optimism': cases and deaths are declining in some hotspots such as Ituri but rising in some health zones, particularly North Kivu, and data do not yet confirm the outbreak has peaked
  • It also called for scaling up the response, especially in North Kivu, addressing community deaths (around 60% of reported deaths), strengthening contact tracing and protecting essential health services
  • Chair Prof. Salim Abdool Karim said sustained interruption of transmission has to be demonstrated before de-escalation is considered

• The EU will not vote on Tesla's FSD (Supervised) on 6 October 2026: the draft agenda for the 119th meeting of the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) lists only a 25-minute "continuation of discussions" on the Netherlands' Article 39 request, and the next scheduled session, in December, is now the earliest date for a bloc-wide vote
  • This supersedes earlier reports that a vote was scheduled for 6 October, and Reuters' earlier line that it was "not expected before October"
  • Approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of the 27 member states representing 65% of the EU population (about 292 million people)
  • The Dutch regulator RDW granted the first EU approval on 10 April 2026 after 18 months of trials, under UN Regulation 171 and an Article 39 exemption in Regulation (EU) 2018/858; the committee has discussed the request twice without voting
  • Seven EU countries have cleared FSD (Supervised): the Netherlands, Lithuania (20 May), Estonia (29 May), Denmark (9 June), Belgium (10 June), Slovenia (7 September) and Czechia (21 September), about 53 million people or roughly 12% of the EU population
  • Germany, France, Italy and Spain remain decisive; France declined to approve the current system over speeding and driver attention but began road-testing two FSD cars after a 2 September call with Elon Musk
  • Sweden's letter to the committee says it will only vote in favour if Tesla removes the speed-offset feature; Norway raised similar concerns
  • Reuters found Tesla pressed RDW from 2024 to keep its safety review confidential; RDW says it did its own testing and did not rely on Tesla's statistics
  • Per Denmark's traffic authorities, an EU rejection would make RDW's provisional approval lapse after six months, invalidating the other national approvals; even if it passes, the regulations need about two years of legislative revision
changes.before:
• The EU's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) is expected to vote on 6 October 2026 on extending the Dutch RDW approval of Tesla's FSD (Supervised) to all 27 member states.
  • The date is reported, not officially set: Reuters says only that a vote could happen in October.
  • It needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of the 27 member states, representing 65% of the EU's population.
  • RDW granted the first EU approval on 10 April 2026 after more than 18 months of testing, under an Article 39 exemption of Regulation (EU) 2018/858 and UN Regulation 171.
  • On 21 September 2026 Czechia recognised the Dutch approval, becoming the seventh EU country after the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium and Slovenia.
  • Those six countries held roughly 8.9% of the EU's population before Czechia joined, far short of the 65% threshold.

  • Reuters found Tesla pressed RDW to keep its safety review confidential; RDW says it relied on its own testing, not Tesla's statistics.
  • A rejection would make RDW's provisional approval lapse after six months, invalidating the national approvals built on it, according to Denmark's traffic authorities.
  • The 6 October TCMV meeting will only continue discussions on the Dutch request; the vote slipped to December at the earliest.

note: The EU vote expected on 6 October will not take place; that TCMV meeting only continues discussions and the next possible vote is in December.

• PAHO's Regional Verification Commission (RVC) will review the measles elimination status of the United States and Mexico in November 2026 at its regular annual meeting
  • The review was first set for a virtual meeting on 13 April 2026 (announced 16 January) and moved on 2 March to November, which CNN reports as a seven-month delay and cancellation of the April special session
  • PAHO says the move simplifies and harmonizes the process and reflects US analysis including complete viral genome sequencing and a bioinformatics platform; an HHS spokesperson said it does not mean the analysis is taking longer than expected
  • The analysis period is one year from outbreak onset: 20 January 2025 in the US and 1 February 2025 in Mexico
  • The RVC is an independent body reporting to the PAHO Director; it assesses whether endemic transmission, meaning the same genotype and lineage circulating uninterrupted for 12 months or more, has been re-established, and recommends a classification to the Director
  • In November 2025 the Americas lost their regional status after the RVC concluded endemic transmission had been re-established in Canada
  • The US national verification committee was to review its evidence in mid-August and send its report to the RVC; its chair writes that Utah's outbreak, begun in June 2025, has apparently run more than 12 months, and that "The U.S. and Mexico may be next"
  • The US had 2,371 measles cases so far in 2026 by early August, more than all of 2025, with 34 new outbreaks and cases reported every week since January 2025
  • Johns Hopkins's William Moss adds that the delay is partly due to CDC staffing and funding shortages, particularly in the measles lab, and that kindergarten MMR coverage has slipped from around 95% to just over 92%

• The WHO South-East Asia Region's target to eliminate measles and rubella reaches its deadline at the end of 2026
  • The goal began in 2013 as measles elimination and rubella control by 2020, was revised to measles and rubella elimination by 2023, after an independent review cautioned the Region was off track, and was then extended to 2026 by the 77th Regional Committee in October 2024, which endorsed a Strategic Plan for 2024-2028
  • The Regional Verification Commission met on 22-23 June 2026 in Colombo, Sri Lanka, its 11th meeting, reviewing all 10 countries' National Verification Committee reports
  • It reported measles outbreaks and rising cases in Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Thailand and Maldives
  • It warned the end-2026 target 'may not be achieved without accelerated and sustained action', citing population immunity gaps, declining funding and the global geopolitical environment
  • It recommended restoring and sustaining coverage above 95% with both doses of measles-containing vaccine in every district, and reaching high-risk groups such as migrants, border populations and conflict-affected communities
  • Where the Region stood: in August 2025 four countries (Bhutan, DPR Korea, Maldives, Timor-Leste) had eliminated measles and six, including newly verified Nepal, had eliminated rubella
  • In 2024 the Regional Committee noted five countries had achieved elimination against the earlier 2023 target

• The 5th International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) runs 23-27 November 2026 at the Addis Ababa Convention Centre in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
  • It is co-hosted by Africa CDC and the Government of Ethiopia, which officially launched it in May 2026
  • The theme is 'Africa's Health Security and Sovereignty: Transformation from Health Dependency and Vulnerability to Ownership and Resilience'
  • It will convene political leaders, policymakers, researchers, innovators, civil society and youth, focusing on reimagining health financing and African-led health security and on reducing dependence on foreign aid
  • Organisers expect 30,000+ attendees and over 100 scientific sessions, and the conference marks '10 Years of Africa CDC'; the inaugural CPHIA in December 2021 drew 2,500 participants
  • The programme includes dialogue with Heads of State, ministers and global health leaders, scientific sessions, innovation and financing showcases and awards for African health research, especially young scientists
  • Announced keynotes include Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director General of Africa CDC, and health ministers of Somalia, Uganda, Sudan and South Sudan
  • Africa CDC invited abstracts and reviewer applications in an August 2026 release, giving an abstract deadline of 15 September 2026, while the conference site gives 30 September 2026 for abstracts, side events, exhibitions and scholarships
  • It builds on CPHIA 2025 in Durban, 'The Durban Promise', and on the Africa Health Security and Sovereignty agenda adopted by the 39th ordinary session of the AU Assembly
  • The previous edition in this list, CPHIA 2023 in Lusaka, drew 5,100 in-person and 30,000 online attendees

  • The nine countries are Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe, with support extended to 12 more

  • Gilead Sciences granted voluntary licences to several manufacturers for generics, and the Global Fund follows a dual-track approach with expanded availability expected 'as early as 2027'
  • South Africa launched lenacapavir on 5 June 2026 as the ninth African country, starting in 360 health facilities; Global Fund supply covers about 456,000 people over two years, far less than needed
  • Gilead's lenacapavir costs about $28,000 per person a year in the US, while a generic is expected in 2027 at around $40 per person per year under a deal covering 120 low- and middle-income countries
  • The $40 price stems from a pricing agreement announced in September 2025 by Unitaid, Wits RHI and CHAI with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories for generic lenacapavir by 2027

  • The meeting is hybrid, participation is by invitation only and onsite attendance is restricted; those not invited can contact the SAGE secretariat
  • The event page lists a draft agenda, declaration of interest, background documents and the SAGE Yellow Book as materials, with presentations to be posted online after the meeting
  • SAGE is charged with advising WHO on overall global policies and strategies for immunization, and meets at least twice a year; its next meetings are listed for 15-18 March 2027 and 27-30 September 2027

• The FDA accepted GSK's New Drug Application for bepirovirsen, an investigational antisense oligonucleotide for adults with chronic hepatitis B, for priority review with a PDUFA goal date of 26 October 2026
  • The FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation, added to Fast Track Designation from February 2024
  • The application rests on the phase III B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials, in 29 countries, which showed statistically significant functional cure rates versus standard of care alone
  • Pooled results: 19% functional cure (233 of 1,220 versus 0 of 614 on placebo) after 6 months of treatment in adults with HBsAg at or below 3000 IU/ml, and 26% (200 of 768 versus 0 of 393) at or below 1000 IU/ml, against about 1% typical with standard of care
  • Functional cure means HBsAg and HBV DNA undetectable for at least 24 weeks after stopping all treatment
  • Most frequent adverse events were injection site erythema, local pain and a temporary rise in a liver enzyme
  • Japan's health ministry approved it as Hibsago on 24 August 2026, the first global approval; GSK said further regulatory decisions, including the US, are expected in the coming months
  • The drug is licensed from Ionis Pharmaceuticals and was, as of April 2026, not approved anywhere in the world
  • It is one of five FDA decisions due in October 2026 in a roundup published 11 September 2026
  • Chronic hepatitis B affects more than 250 million people worldwide and about 1.7 million in the US

  • It has two single-track tubes totalling 4,270 m, running from Otigheim to Niederbuhl under the town of Rastatt, with a top speed of 250 km/h and 15 kV overhead power
  • On 12 August 2017 the eastern-tube tunnel boring machine was entombed after concrete segments shifted under the Rheintalbahn, and DB closed the line above before reopening it in October 2017
  • The eastern tube was then rebuilt by cut-and-cover: demolition of the east-tube ceiling and removal of the machine from spring 2024, and shell construction completed by summer 2025
  • DB switched on the 15,000 V overhead line on the new line in two stages, on 4-5 June 2026 up to Bietigheim and on 10-11 June 2026 for the section to Rastatt Sud including the tunnel, as a step toward operation at the end of the year

• The Tumaini Trial (NCT07842107) is a planned Phase 2/3 adaptive platform trial of candidate Bundibugyo virus vaccines among contacts of cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, not yet recruiting, with an estimated start of 20 October 2026
  • It plans to enrol 3,810 participants, with estimated primary completion in April 2027 and completion in June 2027; the record was posted on 25 September 2026
  • It is co-sponsored by the University of Antwerp and INRB, with CEPI, WHO, the Institute of Tropical Medicine, Epicentre and MSF Belgium as collaborators, and has one site in the DRC
  • Contacts of each confirmed index case form a 'ring'; they are individually randomized on Day 1 to a candidate vaccine or a comparator, and all receive the crossover intervention on Day 29
  • The design is randomized, double-blind and active-controlled; the comparator is a typhoid vaccine, and candidates can be added or dropped for futility under an independent Data Monitoring Committee
  • The candidate is a single-dose Bundibugyo vaccine recommended by WHO's Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccines Prioritization
  • Phase 2 looks at safety through Day 181, and Phase 3 at efficacy against PCR-confirmed symptomatic Bundibugyo virus disease with onset 10 to 29 days after vaccination
  • No vaccine is licensed against Bundibugyo virus; WHO advised on 28 May 2026 that candidate products be used only in clinical trials
  • As of 1 August 2026 the DRC outbreak had 3,748 cases, 1,657 deaths and 708 recoveries, centred on Ituri province, and a 100-bed treatment centre was inaugurated in Bunia
  • On 12 August 2026 WHO said it was in talks on a separate multi-armed Phase 3 trial starting with Merck's Ervebo, with known contacts randomized to Ervebo or placebo, while the registered Tumaini record names a typhoid-vaccine comparator

• Santé publique France's enhanced surveillance of chikungunya, dengue and Zika runs each year from 1 May to 30 November, with regional health agencies in departments where Aedes albopictus is present
  • As of 21 September 2026 (bulletin of 23 September) there were 17 locally acquired transmission episodes: 13 chikungunya with 90 cases (1 to 30 per episode) and 4 dengue with 6 cases (1 to 2 per episode); no new episode versus the previous week
  • Chikungunya episodes were in Tarn, Lot, Gironde, Landes and Val-de-Marne; dengue episodes in Tarn, Herault, Dordogne and Bouches-du-Rhone
  • Imported cases since 1 May: 150 chikungunya, 412 dengue and 15 Zika
  • West Nile virus: 117 locally acquired cases, 25 more than the previous week, including first-ever human cases in several departments
  • Context: between 2004 and 2024 mainland France had only three local chikungunya episodes (2010, 2014, 2017); 2025 saw 809 local cases, the most since enhanced surveillance began in 2006
  • ECDC's week 39 threats report (19-25 September 2026) includes updates on West Nile virus, dengue and chikungunya

  • It targets around 34 lakh (3.4 million) unvaccinated or missed children aged 6 to 59 months
  • The minister announced it on 20 September; children who turn six months during the campaign will also be vaccinated
  • Authorities lowered the minimum vaccination age from the usual 9 months because of the outbreak
  • Why: field data, WHO and Unicef rapid monitoring and hospital data showed some children remained outside coverage, and a significant number of affected children had not received the measles vaccine; the approach this time involves people across villages rather than waiting at vaccination centres
  • The MR programme has run in phases since April, with around 1.98 crore (about 20 million) children vaccinated so far
  • On 13 September the EPI asked all field offices to report within three days how many children aged 6 to 59 months were missed
  • Outbreak scale: 1,087 confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths, including 101 laboratory-confirmed, with nearly 187,000 suspected cases and 21,099 confirmed infections since 15 March; later headlines put the combined toll at 1,096
  • Causes cited: disruptions to routine immunisation in 2024 and 2025 and a nationwide MR vaccine stockout, with no regular nationwide supplementary MR campaigns since 2020
  • WHO's April notice assessed risk as high nationally and regionally and moderate globally, and recommended two doses of measles-containing vaccine and at least 95% coverage

• Agriculture Victoria extended the requirement for targeted poultry biosecurity in southern Victoria by another 28 days from 19 September 2026, until at least 16 October 2026
  • Owners or controllers of 50 or more poultry in southern local government areas, including metropolitan Melbourne, must confine birds to prevent contact with wild birds, their droppings and environments they access; owners elsewhere are recommended to do the same
  • The reason is that H5 bird flu continues to spread among wild birds, largely seabirds and shorebirds along the coastline
  • It is a temporary requirement during an "initial adjustment" to H5 in wild birds, and it will be reviewed against disease activity and risk
  • No H5 detections in poultry or livestock in Australia, and no poultry movement restrictions
  • The ACCC has advised that free-range labelling non-enforcement applies for up to 90 days while a confinement requirement or recommendation is in place
  • The original housing requirement was first introduced for an initial 14 days for owners of 50 or more birds in metropolitan Melbourne, coastal and some neighbouring areas, after 47 positive wild-bird cases
  • H5 was first confirmed on mainland Australia on 20 June 2026, in a brown skua at Cape Le Grand near Esperance, Western Australia
  • Acting Chief Veterinary Officer Cameron Bell listed practical measures: restricting access to higher-risk areas, reducing the area or time birds are outside, improving exclusion from sheds and yards, and protecting feed and water
  • Sick or dead birds should be reported via the Agriculture Victoria website or the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline 1800 675 888

• Question 6, the Right to Abortion Initiative, was an initiated constitutional amendment on the 5 November 2024 ballot and was approved
  • Certified results: 905,170 yes (64.36%) to 501,232 no (35.64%), a total of 1,406,402 votes
  • It would add Article 1, Section 25 to the Nevada Constitution, creating a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability, or when needed to protect the life or health of the pregnant patient
  • Nevada requires initiated constitutional amendments to be approved in two even-numbered election years, so a second vote is set for 3 November 2026
  • Nevada's general election falls on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year
  • Abortion was already legal in Nevada until 24 weeks, following the 1990 Question 7 vote (63.47% to 36.53%)
  • The measure reached the ballot after the 2023 single-subject lawsuit, a Nevada Supreme Court ruling on 18 April 2024 that the text met requirements, and certification on 28 June 2024 with about 128,000 signatures verified; 102,362 valid signatures were needed
  • Supporters (Nevadans for Reproductive Freedom) raised about $13.2 million in total contributions; the opposing Coalition for Parents and Children reported none
  • Yes carried Clark (66.49%) and Washoe (65.88%) counties; No won Lincoln County with 66.22%, its largest share
  • It was one of several abortion measures on 5 November 2024 ballots, approved in seven states and defeated in Florida, Nebraska and South Dakota

  • A yes vote supports a state constitutional right to abortion, with the state able to regulate after fetal viability except where needed to protect the patient's life or health

changes.after: Francis Halzen Wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube
changes.before: The Royal Swedish Academy Names the 2026 Physics Laureates

changes.after: Francis Halzen receives the 2026 physics Nobel for IceCube and the detection of high-energy cosmic neutrinos. The award recognizes a new way to study energetic objects beyond the light they emit.
changes.before: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announces the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics from its Session Hall at Frescati in Stockholm. The prize may be split between up to three laureates.

changes.after:
• The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 physics Nobel to Francis Halzen on 6 October for his role in IceCube and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from astrophysical sources.
  • Halzen is IceCube's principal investigator at UW–Madison. Its sensors occupy a cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice, using rare particle interactions to investigate energetic cosmic objects.
  • The observatory first reported high-energy neutrinos from outside the solar system in 2013. Later detections connected neutrinos to a distant galaxy and revealed emission from an active galaxy and the Milky Way, giving astronomers evidence that light alone cannot provide.
  • The award is to Halzen, while the detector's construction and operation depend on an international collaboration. Speaking from Italy, he credited that collective effort and said he hoped the recognition would support a new proposal.
changes.before:
• The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics is announced on Tuesday, 6 October, "11:45 CEST at the earliest", by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien)
  • The venue is the Academy's Session Hall, Lilla Frescativagen 4A, Stockholm
  • It is the second of six 2026 announcements, which "will take place on 5-12 October", following medicine on Monday 5 October and ahead of chemistry on Wednesday 7 October
  • Like every announcement except the peace prize, the time carries the hedge "at the earliest"
  • All prize announcements "will be broadcast live on the official digital channels of the Nobel Prize", with a YouTube live stream listed for each
  • The Nobel Prize YouTube channel's live stream page for this announcement, "Announcement of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics", was published 2026-09-14T09:20:53Z and says only "The Nobel Prize in Physics will be announced at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, Sweden"; it names no laureates and gives no announcement date
  • A press invitation is listed for the physics announcement, and "Media wishing to attend the announcements should apply to the respective prize-awarding institution in the early fall"
  • The announcement follows a year-long process: nominations open in September, close at "midnight on 31 January", are considered February to September by a Nobel committee of 5 to 10 members, and the prize-awarding institutions "take a final vote to select their newest laureates" in October
  • The laureates receive their medals, prize money and diplomas on Nobel Day, 10 December, in Stockholm and Oslo
  • The schedule was set out in a Nobel Foundation press release dated 2 February 2026; the nobelprize.org announcement-dates page carries no publication or last-updated date
  • None of the three links says how many laureates the physics prize may be shared between

changes.after: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel share the 2026 medicine Nobel for discoveries that allow researchers to control nerve-cell activity with light. Their work links light-sensitive proteins to tools for investigating brain circuits.
changes.before: The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet announces the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine from Wallenbergsalen in the Nobel Forum, opening Nobel week. The announcement is broadcast live and the laureates are usually telephoned only minutes beforehand.

changes.after:
• The 2026 physiology or medicine Nobel was awarded on 5 October to Karl Deisseroth of Stanford, Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University of Berlin and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg.
  • Optogenetics introduces light-sensitive microbial proteins into selected nerve cells, allowing researchers to change those cells' activity with light. This helps test what particular circuits do, rather than simply observe when they are active.
  • The joint award connects investigations of light-gated ion channels with their use in neuroscience. It recognizes a research method and its enabling discoveries, rather than announcing a newly approved treatment.
  • Hegemann's EU-supported research includes work on rhodopsin activation and an ongoing project developing light-controlled molecular switches. A separate collaboration explored an implant combining optogenetics with other approaches for potential Parkinson's applications; that aim remains research, not a clinical outcome.

changes.after: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai share the chemistry Nobel for reactions that amplify one molecular mirror image. Their work explains how chemical handedness can emerge and supports selective pharmaceutical synthesis.

changes.after:
• Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai receive the 2026 chemistry Nobel for discoveries involving non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.
  • The central problem is molecular handedness: two mirror-image forms can have different biological effects, making selective synthesis important for medicines.
  • Kagan's 1986 work showed that reactions could amplify a small imbalance between mirror-image forms; Soai developed an autocatalytic reaction in 1995 and demonstrated formation of a single handed form in 2003.
  • Their experiments offer a chemical route to homochirality, connecting a longstanding question about life's asymmetry with practical methods for pharmaceutical manufacture.
  • The laureates share SEK 12 million equally. Kagan is emeritus at the former Université Paris-Sud; Soai is emeritus at Tokyo University of Science.
  • The announcement belongs to Nobel week; the medals and diplomas are presented on 10 December.

changes.after: Nuri Successfully Launches NEONSAT-2 to 6 on Its Fifth Flight
changes.before: Nuri launches NeonSat-2 to 6

changes.after: South Korea's fifth Nuri flight lifted off at 12:25 KST on 7 October, deploying five NEONSAT spacecraft and nine CubeSats into their target orbits. KASA confirmed normal stage operation and the first NEONSAT ground contact.
changes.before: NeonSat-2 to 6 are part of the South Korean government's Earth observation micro-satellite constellation NeonSat (New-space Earth Observation Satellite). The NeonSat constellation is the first satellite system developed by the government using a mass-production approach for precise monitoring of the Korean Peninsula. Lifts off from LC-2, Naro Space Center, South Korea to Sun-Synchronous Orbit.

changes.after:
• Nuri lifted off from Naro Space Center at 12:25 KST on 7 October 2026. KASA and KARI confirmed five NEONSAT spacecraft and nine CubeSats were separated into their target orbits.
  • The confirmed result replaces the earlier launch forecast: all three rocket stages operated normally, and the fairing separated as planned.
  • NEONSAT-6 made initial contact with the Antarctic King Sejong ground station at about 13:08 KST. The release described subsequent contact attempts for the other spacecraft.
  • The mission used a low-shock separation device and procedures intended to avoid collisions between constellation spacecraft. Greater industrial participation also advances the transition toward commercial launch operations.
  • KASA targets the sixth flight for the second half of 2027, with at least annual launches planned through 2032.
changes.before:
• On 30 September the Korea AeroSpace Administration's chief, Oh Tae-seok, said ‘Preparations have been proceeding without any problems so far’ for the fifth Nuri launch on 7 October from the Naro Space Center in Goheung
  • Nuri will carry 15 satellites: five NEONSAT satellites as the primary payload, forming the country's first domestically launched microsatellite constellation, and 10 CubeSats as secondary payload; Oh called launching different satellites into different orbits ‘a key capability for commercial launch services’
  • KARI's Nuri is set to launch NeonSat-2 to 6 from pad LC-2 at the Naro Space Center in South Jeolla's Goheung County, South Korea, with T-0 at 2026-10-07T03:23:00Z and a window running to 04:23Z
  • Status is “Go for Launch”: “Current T-0 confirmed by official or reliable sources”, following an update of 2026-08-27 reading “GO for launch on October 7”
  • The mission, typed “Earth Science”, goes to Sun-Synchronous Orbit; NeonSat-2 to 6 belong to the South Korean government's Earth observation micro-satellite constellation NeonSat, “the first satellite system developed by the government using a mass-production approach for precise monitoring of the Korean Peninsula”
  • The date has slipped repeatedly since the record was added on 2025-12-09: NET Q3 2026 (2025-12-17), NET September (2026-07-17), “Delayed to NET October” (2026-07-29), then the confirmed 7 October slot
  • The Korea Aerospace Research Institute released a video of the assembly of the rocket's three stages at Naro on the Tuesday before the 30 September report

Notable features

  • Nuri, also known as KSLV-II, is “South Korea's second carrier rocket and the successor to KSLV-1”: three stages, 47.2 m long, 3.5 m across, 200 t at launch, 2,600 kg to LEO, maiden flight 2021-10-21
  • The Nuri configuration stands at 4 launches, 3 successful, 1 failed; operator KARI has 8 launches, 5 successful, 3 failed
